papers.title: Identifying the Genes of Unconventional High Temperature Superconductors
papers.abstract: We elucidate a recently emergent framework in unifying the two families of high temperature (high $T_c$) superconductors, cuprates and iron-based superconductors. The unification suggests that the latter is simply the counterpart of the former to realize robust extended s-wave pairing symmetries in a square lattice. The unification identifies that the key ingredients (gene) of high $T_c$ superconductors is a quasi two dimensional electronic environment in which the d-orbitals of cations that participate in strong in-plane couplings to the p-orbitals of anions are isolated near Fermi energy. With this gene, the superexchange magnetic interactions mediated by anions could maximize their contributions to superconductivity. Creating the gene requires special arrangements between local electronic structures and crystal lattice structures. The speciality explains why high $T_c$ superconductors are so rare. An explicit prediction is made to realize high $T_c$ superconductivity in $Co/Ni$-based materials with a quasi two dimensional hexagonal lattice structure formed by trigonal bipyramidal complexes.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及高温超导理论，与增材制造生物材料方向完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover LPBF, mechanical testing, fatigue, surface roughness, osseointegration, or any biomedical implant context; it is a pure theoretical physics paper on superconductivity.

summary_zh.motivation: 统一铜氧化物和铁基高温超导体的基因。
summary_zh.method: 分析电子结构和晶格结构的特殊排列。
summary_zh.result: 识别出高温超导的关键基因，并预测钴/镍基材料。

summary_en.motivation: To unify the two families of high-temperature superconductors by identifying common genetic features.
summary_en.method: Analysis of electronic structure and crystal lattice arrangements to isolate key ingredients.
summary_en.result: Identified a quasi-2D electronic environment as the gene, and predicted high Tc in Co/Ni-based materials.

papers.title: Three-year follow-up study of health related QOL and lifestyle indicators for Japanese patients after total hip arthroplasty
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Health Sciences, Graduate School of Medicine, Kyushu University, Japan. Electronic address: fujitak@hs.med.kyushu-u.ac.jp

corresponding_authors.name: Kimie Fujita
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Health Sciences, Graduate School of Medicine, Kyushu University, Japan. Electronic address: fujitak@hs.med.kyushu-u.ac.jp

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅关注全髋关节置换术后患者的生活质量和生活方式，未涉及植入物生物力学或有限元分析。
llm.why_not_core: No biomechanics modeling, no stress shielding or micromotion analysis, no FEA, and no comparison of intact vs implanted femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估全髋关节置换术后患者的生活质量和生活方式变化。
summary_zh.method: 对日本患者进行三年随访，收集健康相关QOL和生活方式指标。
summary_zh.result: 术后患者生活质量显著改善，生活方式有积极变化。
summary_zh.validation: 通过患者自报问卷和临床随访进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate changes in health-related quality of life and lifestyle indicators in Japanese patients following total hip arthroplasty over a three-year period.
summary_en.method: A prospective follow-up study collecting patient-reported outcomes and lifestyle data at multiple time points after surgery.
summary_en.result: Significant improvements in quality of life and positive lifestyle changes were observed postoperatively.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up with standardized questionnaires and regular check-ups.
